observations.title: Fake Receiving Signatures Identified
observations.observation:
It was observed that fake signatures of recipients were made on certain vouchers. Please refer Annexure-A. 
Upon further verification, it was noted that key payee details, such as names and dates etc., were not properly mentioned, making it difficult to verify the related claims from the Security Register that records labour entries. Additionally, the dates mentioned on the cash memos and gate register were of May 2025, whereas the original voucher was dated May 2024 (e.g., refer JV-21 dated 24 May 2025). Although the issue was rectified by correcting the date, it highlights a lapse in the system which apparently allowed backdated by almost a year. The detail of vouchers may be referred below:

observations.recommendation: Fake signatures is a serious issue, and management should address the matter with urgency. All vouchers should be supported by properly verified, genuine receiving signatures and complete payee details, including correct names, dates etc., to ensure authenticity and traceability. A verification process should be implemented whereby entries in the cash memos, and visitor log are cross-checked before voucher approval and payment(s). Backdating of vouchers should be avoided, and any corrections should be clearly documented with appropriate justification. Periodic reviews should be conducted to ensure compliance with these procedures. Additionally, the voucher printing date should be recorded on the voucher, in line with standard company practice.

observations.title: Submission of Bogus Bills
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that bogus bills were submitted by Mr. Rehmat Ali. The Accountant, Mr. Rashid Kareem, informed that these bills had been prepared by using blank invoices obtained from the vendors. In one instance, a bill for stay in hotel and meal expenses was claimed using an invoice from an auto workshop. However, these irregularities were never identified by the Accountant. Such bills may be referred as Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: All vouchers should be thoroughly verified before approval to ensure authenticity and accuracy. Bills should be supported by genuine invoices corresponding to the claimed expenses, and any discrepancies or unusual claims should be identified and investigated. Made-up bills obtained from blank invoices is a serious issue, and management should address the matter with urgency. The Accountant should be made responsible for identifying and reporting irregularities. A clear process for entitlement verification, including travel dates etc. should be implemented. Periodic reviews should be conducted to ensure compliance with these procedures.

observations.title: Purchase to Pay Process not Followed
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the Purchase-to-Pay process as required according to the company policies, was not being complied. Key steps such as preparation of Purchase Requisition, issuance of RFQs, collection of minimum 3–5 quotations, preparation of Comparative Statement of Quotations (CSQ), obtaining approvals, and issuance of Purchase Orders were not followed. Non-compliance with the Purchase-to-Pay process weakens transparency, reduces competitiveness, and reduces the control over procurement activities.
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that the Purchase-to-Pay process is fully complied, including requisitioning, RFQs, quotation comparison, approvals, and Purchase Order issuance, to strengthen transparency, competitiveness, and control over procurement activities.

observations.title: Missing Vouchers
observations.observation: Vouchers should be printed, approved, and filed in sequential order in the relevant voucher files. However, during the audit, it was noted that certain BRs and JVs were missing. Upon discussion with the concerned accounts person, it was informed that the printing and filing of BRs and JVs (particularly revenue-related vouchers) were not being properly followed.
observations.recommendation:
According to the policy mentioned as “2. Accounting Operations at Hotel” in the INDEX:
“Hotel Accountant shall be responsible for recording all receipts, payments and relevant entries in the module on daily basis after obtaining approval from the GM Hotel.
Hotel Accountant shall also keep / maintain record of all online and traditional transactions e.g. vouchers, bank reconciliation statements, quotations etc.”

observations.title: Unapproved Vouchers
observations.observation: As per company policy, accountant should obtain approval from the Hotel Manager before posting any voucher in the system. However, it was observed that the accountant at Ambiance Resorts, Hunza was not properly following this procedure. Discussions with the accountant and review of vouchers revealed that approvals were not being properly obtained from the Hotel Manager.
observations.recommendation:
According to the policy mentioned as “2. Accounting Operations at Hotel” in the INDEX;
“Hotel Accountant shall be responsible for recording all receipts, payments and relevant entries in the module on daily basis after obtaining approval from the GM Hotel.”

observations.title: Vouchers Posted Through Irrelevant Voucher Types
observations.observation: During the audit, it was informed by the accountant that vouchers were not properly posted using relevant voucher types. For example, bank payments were posted through Journal Vouchers (JV) instead of Bank Payment Vouchers (BP), and cash payments were also posted through Journal Vouchers (JV) instead of Cash Payment Vouchers (CP). In certain instances, it was observed that the funds transfers were like wise recorded through JV.
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that transactions are recorded using the correct voucher types; Bank Payments through BP, Cash Payments through CP, Bank Receipts through BR, and Journal Vouchers only for adjustments, to maintain proper classification, strengthen internal controls, and ensure accuracy in financial reporting.

observations.title: Voucher Files not Properly Maintained
observations.observation: During the audit, it was informed by the accounts person that voucher files were not being properly maintained. For example, the expense-related vouchers (including booking of expense, payables, payments against payables etc.) were sent to Head Office, without keeping any office record.

observations.title: Missing Cheque Copies with Bank Payment Vouchers

observations.recommendation:

“…… Photocopy of the cheque shall also be attached with the voucher.”

observations.title: Debit Balance Observed in Withholding Income Tax Payable (u/s 155)
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that debit balance of Rs. 3,079,401 was appearing under the account head “Withholding 155” in the Trial Balance dated 02 September 2025. 
Upon discussion, the relevant personnel informed that initially the withholding income tax on leasehold property was booked under Withholding Income Tax Payable u/s 152 (in “Withholding 152 2a – Contracts”) showing a credit balance of Rs. 638,175. Subsequently M/s Arshad Raheem (tax consultant) advised to book in Withholding Tax u/s 155. However, instead of proper adjustment(s) in “Withholding 152 2a – Contracts” the entries were recorded in “Withholding 155”.
During subsequent working it was shared that both the accounts (“Withholding 155” and “Withholding 152 2a – Contracts”) are adjusted accordingly.
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that the accounting entries should be properly recorded.

observations.title: Copy of Generator Rental Contract not Available at Hotel
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that copy of the generator rental contract(s) was not available at the hotel premises. This raises concerns regarding on-site documentation practices and limits the ability of operational staff to verify contractual terms, vendor charges, party obligations, and service details.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that copies of all contracts, including generator should be maintained at the relevant site for reference. Proper documentation ensures compliance, transparency, and ease of verification.

observations.title: Copy of Logbook not Attached with Fuel Bills
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that copy of the logbook was not attached with fuel bills for generators and vehicles, as required under standard practice. The absence of such supporting documents affects the completeness of records and reduces the reliability of verification.
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that as per standard practice, logbook copies are attached with fuel bills, to strengthen documentation and verification.

observations.title: Unapproved Payment for Water Supply
observations.observation:
During the audit it was observed that an amount of Rs. 25,000 was paid for the water supply as “Extraordinary” (i.e. under hand transactions). These payments were approved only by the HM, whereas according to the LFA, any extraordinary or unbudgeted transaction up to Rs. 100,000 should be approved by GM Hotel Operations and Head PM & FP. 
The payment was made in cash through a staff member of Ambiance Resorts, Hunza, who acted as the sole intermediary between the hotel and the service provider. Furthermore, as informed by the relevant accounts person, due to the nature of the transaction, an acknowledgement of receipt or any supporting documentation could not be obtained or attached.
observations.recommendation:
All such payments should be approved in accordance with the authorization limits defined in the LFA. As per clause 6.6 of Limits of Financial Authority:
“Any extraordinary/ unbudgeted transaction upto PKR 100,000 shall be approved by GM Hotel Operations and Head PM & FP”.

observations.title: Balance Confirmation Certificates not Shared
observations.observation: For balance confirmation purposes, the Ambiance Resorts, Hunza was requested for the balance confirmation certificates from the vendors with whom the business activities were done and staff to whom advances were issued (during the audit period). The balance confirmation certificates were awaited till audit completion.
observations.recommendation: For confirmation of payables/receivables recorded in books, the balance confirmation certificates should be provided on timely basis.

observations.title: Repair & Maintenance Log Book not Maintained
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that concerned staff at Ambiance Resorts, Hunza was not maintaining any logbook or register to record repairs, maintenance activities, or changes to fixtures and in-room supplies etc. This lack of documentation makes it difficult to track maintenance, assess the frequency of repairs, monitor equipment performance, and identify recurring issues. As a result, informed decisions regarding the timely replacement of frequently repaired items cannot be made, which may affect guest satisfaction and lead to operational disruptions.
Furthermore, such documentation serves as an important source for verifying vendor bills against reported complaints.
observations.recommendation: The Engineering Department should maintain a proper logbook or register to record all repairs and maintenance activities, including complaint references etc. This will enable tracking of recurring issues, support vendor bill verification, and facilitate timely replacement decisions.

Referred to Head Office

observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that personal files of all employees, including Accounts staff, are maintained and retained in accordance with company standard practice.

observations.title: Handing/Taking Over of Accountant not Conducted
observations.observation:
As per company standard practice, the Handing over/Taking over of “Accountant” should be conducted. During the audit, it was informed by the accountant that he joined in April 2024, but the HOTO was not conducted. 
Referred to Head Office
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that the Handing Over/Taking Over (HOTO) process for the position of Accountant is formally conducted as per company standard practice to maintain continuity of records, safeguard documentation, and ensure smooth transition of responsibilities.
observations.typical_response: We have already adopted formal Handing Over/Taking Over (HOTO) process for the any position vacant in Finance Dept. and you have observed the practical implementation of this practice in Karachi Ambiance

observations.title: Handing Over/Taking Over not Conducted for FA Incharge (Manager Engineering)
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was noted that Mr. Farman, Manager Engineer, who was responsible for overseeing and maintaining fixed assets, joined in June 2025. However, the Handing Over/Taking Over (HOTO) was not conducted at the time of his joining. The absence of a HOTO process increases the risk of gaps in fixed asset records, unclear accountability, and potential issues in safeguarding and managing assets.
Referred to Head Office
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that a proper Handing Over/Taking Over (HOTO) is conducted for the person managing Fixed Assets e.g. in Ambiance Resorts, Hunza it was Manager Engineering.

observations.title: Handing Over/Taking Over not Conducted for HR Personnel
observations.observation:
It was observed that the HR Personnel, transferred from Ambiance Resorts, Hunza in June 2025 (as informed by Accountant – Mr. Rashid Kareem). However, the Handing Over/Taking Over (HOTO) was not conducted. As a result, tracking HR-related documents, e.g. final settlement cases, became difficult, causing delays and operational inefficiencies.
Referred to Head Office
observations.recommendation: It is suggested to implement and comply with a proper handing over/taking over process during staff transfers to ensure continuity, secure documentation, and smooth operations.

observations.title: Visitor Register not Maintained as per Standard Practice
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the Visitor Register was not maintained as per standard practice. A plain register was used instead of a formal visitor log, and key details such as visitor names, CNIC numbers, phone numbers, and signatures were not properly recorded. Time In, and Time Out entries were also inconsistently logged, with no proper matching of arrivals against departures. As a result, the register functioned more as an informal activity log rather than an effective monitoring tool, weakening overall control and traceability of visitor movements.
observations.recommendation: It should be ensured that a formal Visitor Register is maintained as per the company standard practice, capturing complete visitor details for example (but not limited to) CNIC numbers, contact detail, purpose of visit, and Time In/Time Out with signatures, to strengthen monitoring and control of visitor access.

observations.title: Labour Stayed in Hotel Without Proper Authorization and Records
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that labour was allowed to stay in the hotel for work purposes without properly recording their CNIC numbers, retaining copies of CNICs, or obtaining written approval from the Hotel Manager (HM). These workers stayed in the staff area, which has direct access to the lift, thereby providing potential access to the entire hotel, including guest rooms. The lack of proper documentation and authorization, as well as unrestricted access to guest area increases security risks and compromises guest safety.
observations.recommendation: As per standard practice, it should be ensured that all external labour or contractors are properly documented with details (for example, nut not limited to) the CNIC Number, copy of CNIC (where applicable), Phone Numbers etc., approvals are obtained in writing from the HM, and their accommodation is controlled to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive hotel areas, thereby ensuring overall safeguarding, security and guest safety.

observations.title: Incomplete and Unverified Guard Attendance Records
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was noted that the Daily Attendance Record maintained in the “Guard and Ammunition Record” was not available prior to 10th August 2025. As a result, attendance for the preceding period could not be verified. Additionally, attendance was missing for Mr. Noor on 11th, 13th, and 20th August 2025, and for Mr. Rehmat Kareem on 28th August 2025.
Further, as per discussion with the Accountant - Mr. Rashid Kareem, the “Guard and Ammunition Record”, which actually serves as the primary record for marking daily attendance was not matched with the attendance sheet sent to the Head Office for guards’ payment.
Moreover, review of the attendance sheet submitted to Head Office revealed that it was not signed by the Accountant, the Security Supervisor, or the Competent Authority (HM), which weakens its authenticity and reliability.
observations.recommendation: Immediate measures should be taken to ensure that the Daily Attendance Record is properly maintained and reconciled with the attendance sheets submitted to the Head Office. All attendance records should be verified, signed by the Accountant, Security Supervisor, and Competent Authority, and a periodic review system should be implemented to ensure completeness and accuracy.

observations.title: Security Manual / Security Plan Needs to be Devised
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that a formal Security Manual / Security Plan needs to be devised. Such a document will serve as a comprehensive guide including defining the security protocols, ensuring consistency in practices, and enhancing preparedness in handling security-related matters, etc.
Referred to Head Office
observations.recommendation: A formal Security Manual / Security Plan should be developed to outline key security-related areas, the security protocols, standard operating procedures, and response measures, etc. This will also help ensure uniformity in practices and better preparedness for handling security-related matters.

observations.title: No Communication Mechanism Established Among Security Guards
observations.observation: During the audit, it was noted that there was no formal communication mechanism among the security guards. Essential tools and practices such as call signs, whistles, or other means of coordination were not in place. This may hinder effective communication during routine operations and emergencies, potentially compromising overall security effectiveness.
observations.recommendation: It is suggested to establish a proper communication mechanism for security guards, including the use of call signs, whistles, or other suitable tools, to ensure effective coordination and timely response during both, normal and emergency situations.

observations.title: No Security Supervisor in the Hotel
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that the hotel does not have a designated Security Supervisor to oversee security operations. This raises significant concern regarding the management and monitoring of critical security functions such as the control of hotel access points, supervision of security staff, handling and storage of security equipment (including any ammunition), and response to emergencies. The absence of supervisory increases the risk of unauthorized access, procedural lapses, and potential misuse of security resources.
Referred to Head Office
observations.recommendation: A qualified Security Supervisor should be appointed to manage and oversee all aspects of hotel security. The supervisor should be responsible for monitoring staff performance, ensuring adherence to access control procedures, managing security equipment, and conducting regular drills. Their presence will strengthen internal controls, enhance incident response, and ensure a safer environment for guests, staff, and hotel property. Regular training and reporting mechanisms should also be implemented under their supervision.

observations.title: Improper Placement of Luggage X-Ray Machine
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that although a luggage X-Ray machine has been installed at the main entrance for inspection purposes, guest luggage is practically transported through elevators from the lower ground floor to the reception and then moved to the guest rooms without passing through the machine. This indicates either an improper installation of the equipment or non-compliance with the intended inspection process, resulting in potential security risks and ineffective use of resources. Below appended pictures may be referred in this regard:
Entrance
Placement of Luggage X-Ray Machine
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that management review the current placement and utilization of the luggage X-Ray machine to ensure guest luggage passes through the machine for inspection. Proper SOPs should be implemented to strengthen security controls and ensure effective use of the installed equipment.

observations.title: Limitation of X-Ray Luggage Scanner for Standard Baggage
observations.observation:
During the audit, the concerned staff informed that the X-ray luggage scanner is undersized and unable to scan standard suitcases. The height and width clearance of scanner restricts its effectiveness for larger baggage.
Referred to Head Office
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that a baggage scanner with adequate dimensions be installed to accommodate standard-sized suitcases. This will ensure proper screening of luggage, enhance security controls, and prevent potential safety risks arising from unscanned items.

observations.title: Blind Spots of CCTV Cameras
observations.observation:
The installation and coverage of CCTV cameras need to be assessed under the supervision of Head Office. As discussed with the concerned security personnel, current installation of CCTV cameras does not appear to fully cover sensitive areas. Seemingly there were some blind spots inside the building and along the perimeter walls. It is requested to seek expert opinion from the HO Security Department in this regard. Few of the blind spots may include:
Emergency Exit
Roof Top
Accounts Office, Engineering Room
Scrap Dump Area
observations.recommendation: Considering the sensitivity of the matter, it is recommended for a Security Audit, through Support of HO Security Team, to cover all these matters.

observations.title: Unauthorized Access Risk
observations.observation: There was a risk of unauthorized access as the hotel premises do not have proper boundary wall (e.g. at back side). This situation may lead to unauthorized entry, theft, and compromise to guest safety and hotel assets. The emergency exit door also directly opens to the outside area. Below appended pictures may be referred in this regard:
observations.recommendation: It is recommended for a Security Audit, through Support of HO Security Team, to cover all such matters.

observations.title: Entry Record for Labour, Vendor, and Third-Party Personnel etc. not Properly Maintained
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that entry record for labor, vendor, or third-party personnel entering the hotel premises was not being properly maintained. This lack of control poses significant security and safety risks, as unauthorized access cannot be effectively monitored or traced in case of any incident. Further the entry record of labour, and vendors helps in verification of bills, and payment to labour.
observations.recommendation: Entry register should be maintained at the entry point(s), recording essential details such as name, company, purpose of visit, time of entry and exit, and identification proof, etc. Security personnel should be assigned to verify entries and ensure that access is not granted without proper documentation and approval. Regular reviews should be conducted to ensure compliance with these protocols.

observations.title: Un-Approved Gate Passes
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that gate passes were not being authorized by the designated competent authority before the movement of assets, or any other items. This practice weakens control over movement of assets and other related items.
observations.recommendation: All gate passes should be duly approved by the competent authority prior to the movement of assets or any other items, to ensure accountability and safeguard company property.

observations.title: Improper Placement of Water and Sanitation Pipes in Panel Room
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that water and sanitation pipes were installed at the top of the panel room without proper ducting or concealment. This condition creates a potential risk of water leakage, which may lead to electrical short circuits and compromise the safety of equipment as well as overall hotel operations. For visual reference please see below appended pictures:
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended that the water and sanitation pipes above the panel room be properly realigned or enclosed in secure ducting to prevent any exposure to electrical infrastructure. Additionally, preventive insulation and leakage safeguards should be installed to mitigate the risk of short circuits and ensure the safety of equipment and hotel operations.
Food Safety & HACCP
Store Area

observations.title: No Temperature Guns and Monitoring of Chillers Temperature
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that temperature guns were not available for monitoring food storage and transportation temperatures, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. Proper temperature monitoring is crucial to ensure food safety, prevent spoilage, and maintain the cold chain for perishable items. Moreover, the chiller temperatures were not being consistently monitored and recorded, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Proper temperature control is crucial to prevent food spoilage, bacterial growth, and contamination.
observations.recommendation: As per ISO 22000:2018 requirements, calibrated temperature guns should be made available and used for regular temperature monitoring. It is recommended to implement a structured chiller temperature monitoring system, ensuring that readings are taken at defined intervals and recorded systematically. Staff should be trained regarding proper use of temperature monitoring equipment and documentation practices. Additionally, periodic checks should be conducted to verify the functionality and calibration of the devices to maintain compliance with food safety and quality control standards.

observations.title: No Proper Placement of Storage Racks
observations.observation: As per the ISO 22000:2018, proper placement of racks should be ensured. These racks should be away from wall and above from floor. During the audit, it was observed that storage racks in the raw material store were placed directly against the wall, contrary to the recommended practice of maintaining a 16-inch gap.
observations.recommendation: As per standard practice, it is recommended that all storage racks be repositioned to maintain a minimum clearance of 16 inches from the wall. Regular monitoring should be implemented to ensure ongoing compliance with proper storage guidelines.

observations.title: No Inspection of Raw Material & Incoming Vehicle / Missing Certificate of Analysis
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that raw material lots were not inspected in-house, upon receipt. It was also observed that there were no records or checklists available to verify that food transportation vehicles comply with hygiene, temperature control, and safety standards before unloading raw materials.
Furthermore, Certificate of Analysis (COA) is a key requirement for compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and other food safety standards. While suppliers are expected to provide a Certificate of Analysis (COA) for each lot, there was no documented evidence ensuring that COA’s were consistently obtained and verified against internal specification.
observations.recommendation: In accordance with ISO 22000:2018, all incoming raw material lots should undergo mandatory in-house inspection before use. A standardized checklist should be developed and implemented for the inspection of delivery vehicles to ensure compliance with hygiene, temperature, and safety requirements. Additionally, a formal process should be established to ensure that COAs are obtained for every batch, reviewed against internal specifications, and properly documented for traceability.

observations.title: Insects Killers & Rodent Traps Seem to be Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that insect killers and rodent traps were not installed at key entry points and storage areas, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 food safety standards.
observations.recommendation: In line with standard requirements, it is suggested to install rodent traps and insect killers at entry points and storage areas. A comprehensive pest control management system should also be implemented, incorporating scheduled inspections, proper documentation, and defined corrective actions.

observations.title: Food Safety Policy not Displayed
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the Food Safety Policy was not displayed in the store and raw material receiving area, which is a requirement as per food safety ISO 22000:2018 standards. Additionally, there was no evidence of proper communication of the policy to employees.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that the food safety policy be clearly displayed in required places for example the store, and receiving areas etc. Its importance should also be regularly communicated to staff through periodic training sessions, and routine checks should be conducted to ensure continued visibility, awareness, and compliance. Employees should be made fully aware of their individual roles in maintaining food safety.

observations.title: No Separate Area for Rejected Items
observations.observation: According to ISO 22000:2018, non-conforming or rejected items should be properly segregated to prevent accidental use and cross-contamination. During the audit, it was observed that the store does not have a designated material rejection area.
observations.recommendation: As per the ISO 22000:2018 standard it is recommended to establish a dedicated, well-marked material rejection area within the store. Proper signage, clear identification, and staff awareness to facilitate effective handling and segregation of rejected materials should also be ensured.

observations.title: Supplier Evaluation not Conducted
observations.observation: Supplier audits should be conducted as per the requirements of ISO 22000:2018. During the audit, it was observed that there was no structured supplier approval process in place. Additionally, supplier audits were not conducted on a regular basis to ensure compliance with quality and safety standards.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to develop and implement a formal supplier approval process, including predefined criteria for evaluation. Establish a schedule for regular supplier audits to assess compliance, quality standards, and performance as per required ISO 22000:2018 standard.

observations.title: No Defined Raw Material Inspection Criteria
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that there was no defined raw material inspection area in the store, which is a requirement under ISO 22000:2018. The absence of a designated inspection area increases the risk of contaminated, damaged, or non-compliant raw materials being accepted into the production process without proper evaluation.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that clear raw material inspection criteria should be documented, and a proper inspection area should be designated to ensure consistency in quality checks. Additionally, develop a structured procurement system aligned with standard procurement requirements, including supplier evaluation, material specifications, and approval processes.

observations.title: Material Safety Data Sheet Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) were not available for the cleaning chemicals stored in the facility, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and general good food safety regulations. MSDS documents are essential for ensuring safe handling, storage, and emergency response procedures for hazardous substances.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to ensure that MSDS for all cleaning chemicals are readily available in the store. Train staff on the safe handling and usage of chemicals as per the provided safety guidelines. Conduct regular checks to ensure compliance with chemical safety regulations.

observations.title: No Proper Documentation Available for Cleaning & Sanitation
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that proper cleaning and sanitation procedures were not in place, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. A structured cleaning and sanitation program is essential to prevent cross-contamination, microbial growth, and food safety hazards.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to develop and implement a standardized cleaning and sanitation procedure, including clear guidelines on cleaning frequency, approved chemicals, proper methods, and responsible personnel etc. Staff should be trained accordingly, and proper records of cleaning activities should be maintained to ensure accountability and compliance.

observations.title: No Segregation of Food and Non-Food Material
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that food and non-food items were stored together without proper segregation, and there were no designated racks to separate them, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Proper segregation is essential to prevent cross-contamination and ensure food safety.
observations.recommendation: As per ISO 22000:2018 it is recommended that designated separate, clearly labelled racks should be installed for food and non-food items to prevent cross-contamination. Implementation of storage guidelines that ensure proper segregation is also recommended, along with staff training to emphasize the importance of maintaining food safety standards.

observations.title: Medical Tests of Store Staff Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that medical tests of store staff were either not conducted or not properly documented, as no evidence of medical test records was available. This constitutes non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. Ensuring that all food-handling personnel are medically fit is essential to prevent potential food contamination and safeguard consumer health and safety.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that management should ensure all store staff undergo mandatory medical tests at regular intervals as per food safety regulations in accordance with the ISO 22000:2018 requirement. Proper records of medical check-ups and fitness certificates should also be maintained.

observations.title: HACCP Documentation Found to Be Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) documents were not available, and there was no evidence of its implementation, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that management should develop and implement a comprehensive HACCP plan covering hazard identification, critical control points (CCPs), monitoring procedures, corrective actions, and record-keeping. Furthermore, relevant staff should be trained on HACCP principles, and ongoing compliance should be ensured through regular reviews and updates of related documentation.

observations.title: Non-Compliance with Allergen Management Requirements
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that allergens were not properly segregated, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. There were no clear procedures for identifying, handling, or segregating allergenic ingredients.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to develop and implement a structured allergen management system, including proper labeling, storage segregation, and handling procedures for allergenic ingredients. Training should also be provided staff on allergen control measures, and establish clear documentation and monitoring processes to ensure compliance.
Main Kitchen

observations.title: Visitor Entrance Protocols not Found in Kitchen
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that visitor entrance protocols were not properly implemented, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Visitors were not required to follow specific hygiene and safety measures before accessing food preparation areas.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that hotel management should develop and implement a visitor entrance protocol, including mandatory hygiene practices such as wearing protective gear, handwashing, and signing a visitor log under the guidelines of ISO 22000:2018.

observations.title: No Allergens Mentioned in Menu
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that allergens were not mentioned in the menu, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. There were no indications or labels identifying potential allergens in food items.
observations.recommendation: As per ISO 22000:2018 it is recommended to update the menu to clearly indicate allergen information for each dish. Symbols or labels to highlight common allergens such as nuts, dairy, gluten, and seafood should be used. Training should be provided to staff on allergen awareness and ensure proper documentation is maintained for compliance with food safety standards.

observations.title: Unavailability of Training Records
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that training records for employees were not available which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. There was no documented evidence of staff training on food safety, hygiene, or operational procedures.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to implement a structured system for recording and maintaining employee training, ensuring that all staff members receive regular training in food safety, hygiene, and other relevant areas. Up-to-date training logs should be maintained for all employees, and the training process should be periodically reviewed to ensure compliance with industry standards.

observations.title: Use of Non-Food-Grade Wooden Utensils in Food Handling Areas
observations.observation: It was observed that non-food-grade wooden utensils were being used in food handling areas, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 & HACCP. Since wooden materials are porous in nature, they can absorb moisture and harbor bacteria and other contaminants, thereby posing a significant risk to food safety.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to replace all wooden kitchen items e.g. Spoons, Spatula, Cutting Boards , and Wooden Dishes etc. with food-grade, non-porous alternatives such as stainless steel or food-safe plastic as per ISO22000:2018 requirements. Policy prohibiting the use of wooden utensils and surfaces in food preparation areas should be implemented.

observations.title: Chillers Temperature not Being Monitored
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that chiller temperatures were not being consistently monitored and recorded, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements. Temperature control is critical for preventing bacterial growth and ensuring food safety.
observations.recommendation: As per ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements it is recommended to implement a structured temperature monitoring system for all chillers. Designated staff should be assigned to monitor and record chiller temperatures at defined intervals to ensure proper food storage conditions and early detection of temperature deviations. It is further recommended to use calibrated temperature monitoring devices and maintain logs for compliance.

observations.title: Non-Maintenance of Mandatory Food Safety Records and Logs
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that record-keeping for food safety processes was not in place, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements. Kitchen staff do not maintain any record forms related to food safety, hygiene, cleaning schedules, temperature logs, or other critical operational procedures.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to implement a structured record-keeping system in accordance with ISO standards to ensure that all critical records, such as temperature logs, cleaning schedules, food preparation checklists, and hygiene records, are maintained daily.
Required Documentation

observations.title: Missing Required Documents
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that essential documentation required for ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP compliance was missing. The following critical documents were not found:
Drinking water and process water testing reports from an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved laboratory, covering physiochemical, heavy metals, and microbiological parameters.
Wastewater testing reports for physical and chemical parameters.
Complete documentation of food safety management system, including:
Policies and Procedures
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
Monitoring Record Sheets
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to:
Arrange water quality testing from an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved lab and maintain updated reports. 
Conduct wastewater testing and ensure compliance with environmental regulations. 
Develop and implement food safety documentation, including policies, SOPs, and monitoring records. 
Train staff on documentation requirements and ensure proper record-keeping for audits and regulatory compliance. Regularly review and update food safety documents to align with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP standards.

observations.title: Environmental & Engineering Monitoring Process not in Place
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that environmental and engineering monitoring processes were not in place, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. The following critical parameters were not documented or monitored:
Light Intensity: Section-wise assessment missing.
Noise level: No section-wise monitoring records.
Temperature and Humidity: No documented tracking.
Air Quality Monitoring: Not conducted or recorded.
Generator Stack Emission: No testing or compliance records.
Boiler Stack Emission: Monitoring records not available.
Workers’ Hand Swab Testing: No microbiological testing records.
Processing Equipment Swab Testing: No hygiene validation.
Electrical DBs (Distribution Boards): No inspection or safety records.
Boiler Inspection: No preventive maintenance or safety audit found.
Lift Inspection: No compliance records or maintenance logs.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to:
Implement a structured Environmental & Engineering Monitoring covering all listed parameters. 
Conduct yearly light, noise, temperature, humidity, and air quality assessments and maintain records. 
Perform generator and boiler stack emissions testing to comply with environmental regulations. 
Establish microbiological swab testing protocols for workers' hands and processing equipment. 
Conduct periodic electrical DB, boiler, and lift inspections with proper documentation. 
Train staff on safety and hygiene monitoring and assign responsibilities for maintaining records. 
Ensure all monitoring activities are reviewed periodically for continuous improvement and compliance.

observations.title: Calibration of Measuring and Monitoring Devices not Done
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the calibration of monitoring and measuring devices and equipment had not been conducted which is non-compliance of ISO 22000:2018. Additionally, there was no evidence of calibration records from an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved laboratory.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to:
Schedule calibration for all monitoring and measuring devices (e.g., thermometers, weighing scales, air quality meters, humidity sensors, pH meters) through an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved lab. 
Maintain calibration certificates and records for all critical equipment. 
Implement a calibration schedule to ensure regular monitoring and compliance. 
Train relevant staff on the importance of calibration and ensure proper documentation is maintained for audits and regulatory compliance. 
Conduct periodic internal audits to verify that calibration records are updated and all equipment functions within acceptable limits.

observations.title: Non-Compliance in Laboratory Testing of Raw and Final Products
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that final and raw material analysis was not being conducted from an external ISO 17025-accredited laboratory, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. Regular testing of raw materials and final products is essential to ensure food safety, quality, and compliance with regulatory standards.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to conduct regular external laboratory testing from an ISO 17025-accredited lab for the following:
Raw Material Analysis: (Twice a Year)
Fruits & Vegetables: Pesticide residues & heavy metals.
Meat Products: Microbiological analysis.
Dairy Products: Proximate & microbiological analysis.
Dry Food Items (Spices, Pulses, etc.): Aflatoxins, microorganisms, pesticides.
Final Product Analysis: (Quarterly)
Cooked & uncooked food testing on a quarterly basis.
Comprehensive microbiological analysis.
Proper documentation of all test reports should also be ensured for regulatory compliance and traceability.
Others

observations.title: Logbook for Pool Bike not Maintained
observations.observation: Logbook for pool vehicles should be maintained. During the audit, it was observed that the Ambiance Resorts, Hunza was not maintaining the logbook for pool motorbike.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to ensure that logbooks are properly maintained with KM records, traveler signatures, POL drawn and maintenance details, free from cutting / overwriting, and duly verified by relevant personnel.

observations.title: Vehicle (BRV) Log Book not Properly Maintained
observations.observation:
Vehicle log book should be maintained as per company standard practice. During the audit, certain discrepancies were observed in maintaining logbook for pool vehicle (BRV). Such as:
KM’s not calculated.
Not properly signed by travelers.
Maintenance/ Repairs/ Out of order of instances not recorded in Logbook.
POL drawn not properly mentioned.
Cutting / Overwriting observed in certain instances.
Not verified / validated by relevant personnel.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to ensure that logbooks are properly maintained with KM records, traveler signatures, POL drawn, and maintenance details, free from cutting / overwriting, and duly verified by relevant personnel.

observations.title: Water Bowser Log Book not Properly Maintained
observations.observation:
Log book should be maintained as per company standard practice. During the audit, certain discrepancies were observed in maintaining logbook for water bowser. Such as:
KM’s not calculated.
Maintenance/ Repairs/ Out of order of instances not recorded in Logbook.
POL drawn not properly mentioned.
Not verified / validated by relevant personnel.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to ensure that logbooks are properly maintained with KM records, signatures, POL drawn and maintenance details, free from cutting / overwriting, and duly verified by relevant personnel.

observations.title: Generators Log Book not Properly Maintained
observations.observation:
Generator log book should be maintained as per company standard practice. During the audit, certain discrepancies were observed in this regard. Such as:
No record available before June 2025. 
Not verified / validated by relevant personnel.
Runtime, and Running Hours columns not filled e.g. in August 2025.
Not signed by generator operator, while ON/OFF.
Diesel filled not recorded on the log book.
Maintenance/ Repairs/ Out of order of instances not recorded in Logbook.
Maintained on loose papers, instead of a binded form, as per company practice.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to ensure that logbooks, including generator records, are properly maintained with accurate runtime details, required signatures, fuel filled, maintenance entries, free from cutting / overwriting, and duly verified by relevant personnel. Further it should be maintained in a binded form, as per company practice.

observations.title: Fuel Average Monitoring not Conducted
observations.observation: As per company standard practice, monitoring of generator fuel averages should be ensured. However, during the audit it was observed that generator fuel consumption was not being properly monitored. This lapse may result in untracked variances in fuel efficiency, leading to potential wastage and higher operating costs.
observations.recommendation:
As per company practice, regular monitoring and documentation of generator fuel averages should be ensured, to track efficiency, identify variances, and control fuel-related costs.
Fuel Average = Fuel Consumption ÷ Running Hours

observations.title: Google Mini and Nest Devices not Properly Configured
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that Google Mini and Google Nest devices installed in guest rooms were not properly configured. As per the concerned person, in the event of power switching, due to load shedding or changeover to generator/UPS, the devices automatically reset and their configurations are erased. As a result, the devices were not functioning effectively and guests were unable to fully utilize the facility.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that the devices be properly installed with backup configurations.

observations.title: Missing Information in Guest Folios (Opera)
observations.observation:
During the audit review of guest folios, several critical details were found missing, raising concerns about billing accuracy, record-keeping, and compliance with hotel policies. Despite the implementation of the Opera system on November 7, 2024, the following discrepancies were observed in system-generated guest folios:
Guest names were not appearing on guest folios.
Check-in and check-out times were missing.
Room category and the number of guests (pax) were not recorded, which directly impacts the rate charged.
System-generated guest folio numbers were not appearing.
Guest folio print dates and user detail were not available on the footer of the printed folios.
Moreover, guest and cashier signatures are also not available on the folios. Detailed list of identified issues is provided in Annexure-A.
observations.recommendation: The Front Office (FO) should make sure that all guest folios are properly filled out, including guest signatures, cashier signatures, check-in and check-out times, guest names, and folio numbers. To prevent these mistakes in the future, regular checks should be done, and staff should be trained to follow the correct process.

observations.title: Early Check-In and Late Check-Out Charges not Applied
observations.observation:
During the audit, multiple instances of early check-ins and late check-outs were observed where applicable as per the policy: 
“25% of room rent as late check-out charges till 14:00hrs, 50% charges till 15:00hrs and full night charges thereafter.” 
“Previous night charges may apply if check-in is requested prior to 12:00 noon which will always be subject to availability” 
These charges were neither billed nor collected from guests. Additionally, approval for waiving the additional charges was also not attached to the guest folios. Some of the instances are provided in Annexure-B
observations.recommendation: The Front Office (FO) must ensure that early check-in and late check-out charges are correctly applied as per company policy. In cases where a waiver is granted, proper approval must be obtained and attached to the guest folio.

observations.title: Discrepancies Found in Guest Refund Payments
observations.observation:
During the audit review of refund cases, several critical irregularities were identified, indicating weaknesses in the refund process. These findings indicate a lack of financial control and transparency in the refund process, increasing the risk of errors, misappropriation, and financial misstatement. Strengthening approval mechanisms, ensuring proper documentation, and improving system-based tracking are essential to addressing these issues. Key findings are as follows:
Lack of Proper Authorization and Documentation
Most refund slips are not signed by the Guest, Duty Manager, or Cashier, compromising the authenticity of transactions.
Guest details, including names, are missing from refund slips, making it difficult to verify the legitimacy of refunds.
Inconsistent and Non-Transparent Refund Processing
Guest refunds are being issued in cash rather than through the original payment mode. 
Refunds are also processed using Paid Out Slips without proper approvals.
Improper Handling of Refund Payable Ledger
The refund payable ledger is closed daily in both Opera and BEAMS, resulting in a nil balance in BEAMS. However, unprocessed refund cash remains with the accounts department instead of being properly accounted for.
Refund transactions are being manually tracked in an Excel sheet, increasing the risk of errors and mismanagement.
Mismanagement of Unprocessed Refund Cash
It has been observed that unprocessed refund cash is being deposited into accountant personal bank account rather than a designated company account for guest refunds. 
As of January 31, 2025, the outstanding refund payable balance is PKR 527,698, which is not reflected in the system reports. The month-wise details of the refund payables are provided in Annexure-C.
Irregularities in Refunds During Guest Check-Out
In certain cases, excess amounts were received from guests at check-out and immediately refunded. Instance are given in Annexure-C
This practice was commonly observed in late check-out cases, raising concerns about possible errors or deliberate mismanagement in billing and refunds.
observations.recommendation:
To enhance transparency and control, guest refunds should be processed using the original payment mode, with a defined threshold for cash refunds. All refund slips must be properly authorized and signed by the Guest, Duty Manager, and Cashier, with guest details clearly recorded. The refund payable ledger should accurately reflect outstanding balances, and system-generated reports must replace manual Excel tracking. 
Additionally, unprocessed refund cash must be deposited into the company's designated bank account to prevent mismanagement.
The accountant should be required to provide clarification regarding the approval and rationale for holding the refund payable amount in a personal account. Additionally, it should be ensured that such amounts are deposited into the company's official bank account in compliance with financial policies.

observations.title: Lack of Proper Authorization & Details Missing in Paid Out Slips
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that several Paid-Out Slips were missing essential details, raising concerns about accuracy and transparency. Many slips were not signed by the guest, Duty Manager, or Cashier, and key guest details, such as the guest's name and the purpose of the paid-out transaction, were not recorded. 
Additionally, discrepancies were identified in the recorded time of paid-out transactions, where the slip time did not match the attached supporting documents, such as Indriven screenshots. 
Furthermore, the footer section of some Paid Out Slips was incomplete, missing critical information like the user and print time. Some of the instances are given below:
observations.recommendation: All Paid Out Slips must be properly filled out, including guest details, purpose, and signatures from the guest, Duty Manager, and Cashier. The recorded time should match supporting documents, and the footer must include user and print time. Regular checks should be conducted to ensure accuracy and prevent unauthorized transactions.

observations.title: Guest Registration Crad not Prepare by FO
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the Front Office (FO) did not prepare the Guest Registration Card (RC) at the time of guest check-in. As per standard procedure, the RC must be prepared and signed by guests upon check-in, as it formally documents key terms and conditions, including policies on early check-in, late check-out, and other relevant charges. Failure to follow this process may result in billing disputes, non-compliance with hotel policies, and potential financial and operational risks.
observations.recommendation: Front Office (FO) must prepare the Guest Registration Card (RC) and obtain guest signatures upon check-in. Additionally, FO staff should verbally communicate the key terms and conditions outlined in the RC to enhance guest awareness and prevent disputes.

observations.title: Recordkeeping of BTC Client Data Outside Opera System
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that BTC client data has not been maintained in the Opera system since its go-live on November 7, 2024. Instead, the accountant has been recording BTC client data in Excel.
Additionally, receipts from BTC clients for outstanding amounts in Munshi were recorded in Munshi, while receipts related to receivables after November 7, 2024, were maintained in Excel. It was also observed that the City Ledger balance for BTC clients in Opera remains nil, as the accounts department has continued to manage records outside the system. This practice increases the risk of errors, inconsistencies, and financial mismanagement.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that BTC client data be fully integrated into the Opera system to ensure accurate financial reporting and centralized record-keeping. observations.title: Guest Folios of BTC Clients not Available in Hotel
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was found that guest folios for BTC (Bill to Company) clients, signed by the BTC guests, were not available at the hotel. The accountant stated that these folios were sent to BTC clients, and no copies were kept at the hotel. Keeping signed guest folios at the hotel is important for proper record-keeping and avoiding disputes. Without these records, the hotel may face the following risks:
Billing Disputes: If a BTC client questions a charge, there is no signed proof to confirm the billing details.
Payment Issues: Missing folios can lead to delays or non-payment, as there is no official record to support the charges.
observations.recommendation: The hotel accountant should ensure that duplicate copies of all signed guest folios for BTC (Bill to Company) clients are properly maintained at the hotel before sending the originals to clients. This will help prevent billing disputes, support timely payment collection, and improve financial record-keeping.

observations.title: Balances of Munshi not Transfer in Opera (Receivables and Advances)
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that the opening balances of BTC (Bill to Company) client receivables from Munshi were not uploaded into the Opera system. As of February 12, 2025, the outstanding receivables recorded in Munshi amounted to PKR 7.922 million. Since receipts from BTC clients against these receivables continue to be recorded in Munshi.
Furthermore, advances received from guests, amounting to PKR 4.44 million as per the Munshi report dated November 7, 2024, were also not transferred to Opera. The accountant confirmed that these advance balances were not uploaded into the system, and no records of advances are available in Opera. This gap in data migration poses risks of financial discrepancies, mismanagement, and potential loss of funds.
observations.recommendation: The hotel should ensure that all outstanding BTC client receivables and guest advance balances from Munshi are accurately transferred to the Opera system. BTC client receipts should also be recorded in Opera to maintain a centralized and transparent financial record. Proper reconciliation between Munshi and Opera should be conducted to prevent discrepancies, improve financial management, and minimize the risk of misstatements.

observations.title: Sale Cash Used by Front Office for Expenses
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that front office staff were utilizing sale cash for various purposes, including guest refunds, paid outs, and covering petty or urgent expenses. Instead of following the proper procedure of requesting funds through a Front Office Impress, sale cash was directly used, bypassing standard financial controls. This practice can lead to several financial and operational risks.
observations.recommendation: The front office should not use sale cash for guest refunds, paid-outs, or petty expenses. Instead, all such transactions should be processed through an approved Front Office Impress system with proper authorization and documentation. A designated impress fund should be maintained for front office expenses, ensuring accurate recording and reconciliation

observations.title: Bank Reconciliation not in Practice both at Hotel and Head Office
observations.observation:
The absence of proper bank reconciliations poses a significant risk to financial accuracy, internal controls, and transparency, potentially leading to undetected errors, misstatements, or fraudulent activities.
During the audit, it was found that bank reconciliations were not maintained at the hotel for the collection accounts held with Askari Bank and MCB Bank. Upon inquiry, the hotel accountant stated that bank reconciliations are only prepared at the Head Office; however, the Head Office has not provided the required reconciliations for the audit period from July 2023 to December 2024.
observations.recommendation: To mitigate financial risks and ensure compliance with the best practices, it is recommended that bank reconciliations be prepared and maintained regularly at the hotel level and made available for audit review in a timely manner.

observations.title: Revenue Reconciliation not in Practice
observations.observation:
During the audit it was observed that revenue reconciliations are not prepared at either the hotel or Head Office level, which raises concerns regarding the accuracy and completeness of the reported revenue from various sources, including room sales, café sales, and ancillary services.
The lack of revenue reconciliation poses a significant risk to financial accuracy, revenue tracking, and internal controls and increases the likelihood of misstatements, revenue leakage, unverified financial records, and potential fraud.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that revenue reconciliations be conducted regularly at both the hotel and Head Office levels for all revenue streams, including room sales, café sales, and ancillary services, to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and transparency of reported revenue.

observations.title: Use of a Shared Bank Account for Revenue Collection
observations.observation: Ambiance Karachi operates three bank accounts, including an Askari Bank account (No. 3491650000248), which is used for revenue collection from both Ambiance Lahore and Karachi. The shared use of this account impedes accurate revenue segregation between the two locations, leading to challenges in proper identification and allocation. Consequently, this impacts the accuracy of financial reporting and reconciliation.
observations.recommendation: To ensure accurate revenue segregation and enhance financial reporting, separate bank accounts should be maintained for Ambiance Karachi and Ambiance Lahore. If a shared account is unavoidable, a structured revenue allocation mechanism and automated tracking should be implemented.

observations.title: Incomplete Information/Documentation in Cash Drop Envelopes
observations.observation: During the audit, it was found that cash drop envelopes from the Front Office and Café were missing important information, creating risks for cash reconciliation and financial transparency. Several envelopes lacked a cash summary and monetary details, while many were missing signatures and ID details of the Shift Cashier, Witness, and General Cashier. Additionally, the outlet name (Front Office or Café), shift timing, and dates were not recorded on some envelopes, and denomination breakdowns were incomplete.
observations.recommendation: All cash drop envelopes should include a cash summary, denomination details, and complete monetary breakdowns. The Shift Cashier, Witness, and General Cashier must sign and provide their ID details. Each envelope should also clearly mention the outlet name, shift timing, and date. These steps will help improve cash tracking, ensure accuracy, and maintain financial transparency.

observations.title: Calculation Errors in Cash Drop Envelopes
observations.observation: During the audit, calculation errors were identified in a few cash drop envelopes from the Front Office and Café. Total cash recorded on the envelope did not match the cash denominations listed. Additionally, these discrepancies were not identified or flagged by the accounts department. Such errors highlight weaknesses in cash handling procedures and increase the risk of financial mismanagement, cash shortages, and reconciliation issues. Instances are given below:
observations.recommendation: To improve cash handling procedures, shift cashiers must verify that the total cash amount recorded on the envelope matches the denomination breakdown before submission. Dual authentication should be enforced by requiring signatures from both the Shift Cashier and a Witness. The accounts department must conduct regular checks on cash drop envelopes to identify discrepancies and report issues promptly.

observations.title: Discrepancies Founds in Guest Advance Deposit Slips
observations.observation: During the audit, several issues were found in advance deposit slips given to guests, affecting accuracy and clarity. In some cases, the deposit time on bank transfer slips was later than the time on system-generated receipts, making it hard to match records and verify payments. Guest names were also missing, which could lead to confusion and disputes. Additionally, the report header showed "Oracle Hospitality" instead of the hotel’s name, which might cause misunderstandings.
observations.recommendation:
All advance deposit slips should include complete and accurate details, including guest names for proper verification. The issue related to the transaction time on advance deposit slips should be identified—if it is a system error, it must be resolved immediately. If front office staff issue deposit slips before receiving the actual advance, the matter should be investigated and corrected. Additionally, the report header should be updated by Head Office to display the hotel's name “Ambiance” instead of "Oracle Hospitality" to avoid confusion.

Clubbed quantities and activities.

Detailed Aspects of the Assets were not mentioned.
These hindrances were communicated with respective personnel in the HO, but, satisfactory response and support was not received timely. Instances are given in Annexure-D
observations.recommendation:

Excel lacks proper tracking of changes, increasing the risk of errors and unauthorized modifications.

Be maintained in a system that allows tracking of updates and changes.
Clearly mention the quantity and unique asset number of each asset to facilitate verification.
Ensure that only assets meeting the capitalization threshold are included in the Fixed Asset Register, while those below the threshold should be recorded in a separate memorandum stock register.
Include detailed descriptions, specifications, and serial numbers where applicable to improve asset identification.

observations.title: Incomplete FA Inventory Register – Unrecorded Paintings (PKR 5.4 Million)
observations.observation: The Fixed Asset Register should account for all items considered fixed assets with a capitalizable value (10,000 and above). During the physical verification, it was observed that valuable paintings (some located in rooms and other areas of the hotel building) were not included in the hotel’s Fixed Asset Inventory Register. Omitting such significant assets from the cost capitalization process appeared both unjustifiable and concerning.
observations.recommendation: Fixed Asset Register should be complete in all respect including all and every kind of Fixed Assets of Capitalizable value (10,000 and above). Detailed stock count is suggested under supervision of fixed asset department resulting in subsequent updating of fixed asset register.

observations.title: Physical Verification of Fixed Assets not Conducted
observations.observation: As per best practices and to ensure the completeness of asset records, a physical verification of fixed assets should be conducted at least once a year. However, during the audit, it was found that a formal and detailed verification of fixed assets had never been performed at the hotel since its inception. The absence of regular verification increases the risk of missing, misplaced, or unaccounted assets, leading to weak asset management and control.
observations.recommendation: The Head Office Finance team should ensure that a formal physical verification of fixed assets is conducted at least once a year. The verification process should be properly documented, and discrepancies, if any, should be investigated.

observations.title: Fixed Asset Codes/Tags not Provided by HO
observations.observation:
All fixed assets should have a unique number or tag for proper tracking, recording, and verification. However, during the physical inspection, it was found that all assets did not have fixed asset tags or codes. Upon inquiry, it was revealed that the Head Office had not provided asset tags for labelling the assets. 
As per FHS fixed asset policy, “Each asset shall be assigned unique fixed asset code. However, in case of similar assets procured in large quantity e.g. chairs, tables, vases, mattresses etc. “type/sub-category” may be assigned one asset code (instead of assigning code to every item). Total quantity of such type of assets shall be accounted for in the system”.
observations.recommendation: The Head Office Finance Team should ensure that all fixed assets are assigned unique asset codes and properly tagged as per FHS fixed asset policy. Asset tags should be provided to the hotel for labelling and proper identification of all assets. Implementing this practice will improve asset tracking, enhance verification procedures, and strengthen internal controls over fixed assets.

observations.recommendation: The hotel manager should ensure that all unusable items, including discarded linen, are reported to the Head Office for disposal in a timely manner through the Asset Inspection & Disposal Note (AIDN). observations.title: Errors and Discrepancies in System-Generated Stock Inventory Report
observations.observation:

“Delivery Charges" (ST-423) was wrongly included in the store inventory report.
Multiple codes were open for the same item, such as Energizer Cell AA and Milk Pack Cream 200ml.
Some items lacked important specifications, e.g., the weight of the Pringles, Kit Kat, and Mars did not mention.
Some items had no unit of measurement, while others had incorrect units also mentioned against some item e.g., Samsung/Haier remote listed in KG.
Some items appeared with negative quantities, such as Choco Bliss (-1), Dadi Jan Papri (-2), and K&Ns Tender Breast Chicken 700G (-20).
observations.recommendation: The store inventory report should be reviewed and corrected to address the errors highlighted in the audit. A proper system should be implemented to prevent duplicate codes, incorrect units, and negative stock balances.

observations.title: Non-Compliance of Procurement Policy (PR, PO & GRN not in Practice)
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was found that key procurement documents, including Purchase Requisition (PR), Purchase Order (PO), and Goods Receipt Note (GRN), were not being used in the hotel's procurement process. These documents are essential for verifying order quantity, quality, and authorization.
Moreover, it was observed that routine purchases were made from local vendors instead of well-known market vendors such as Hyperstar, Imtiaz, and Metro.
observations.recommendation:
The procurement process should include mandatory preparation of Purchase Orders (PO) based on Purchase Requisitions (PR) and Goods Receipt Notes (GRN) based on delivery challans.
As per FHS Policy “PR shall be required for all the transactions amounting to PKR 5,000 and above” and “Goods received, inspected and accepted shall be documented through Goods Received Note (GRN)”.
As per FHS Procurement policy section “Sourcing for Routine Procurement” “For routine procurements, specific vendors such as Hyperstar, Metro, Alfatah, Imtiaz Super Store etc. shall be preferred. In this regard running rate contracts shall be made with them by SC department”.

observations.title: List of Common/Register Vendors not Available at Hotel
observations.observation: List of common suppliers and register vendors should be available in the hotel for convenience of procurement and deduction of applicable income tax across the board. It was observed during the audit the said information was not available in the hotel.
observations.recommendation: List of common and registered suppliers should be available in the hotel for the convenience of procurement and deduction of applicable Income Tax.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Kitchen Inventory
observations.observation: During the stock audit, it was found that kitchen inventory requisitions were not handled by the store Incharge. Instead, the Chef placed orders directly with vendors, who delivered the items straight to the kitchen instead of the store. As a result, proper issuance from the store to the kitchen was not followed. Additionally, the store Incharge updated the kitchen inventory in the system only once a month, based on records provided by the Chef.
observations.recommendation:
All requisitions related to the kitchen should be routed through the store Incharge to ensure proper record-keeping and control. Vendors should deliver items to the store first, and the store Incharge should issue them to the kitchen as per approved requisitions. Additionally, kitchen inventory should be recorded in the system on a real-time or daily basis to maintain accurate stock records.

Install additional cameras in the uncovered zones, especially in high-risk or sensitive areas, to enhance surveillance. Regular assessments of the camera system should be carried out to identify any new blind spots and ensure the system remains effective.

observations.title: Discrepancies Regarding Luggage X-Ray Machine
observations.observation:
During Fixed Asset Inspection and Verification exercise following discrepancies were found with Luggage X-Ray Machine installed at screening room entrance of the hotel. These discrepancies were discussed and confirmed by Mr. Raja Muhammad Younus (Security Supervisor) as well.
X-RAY Machine (Luggage) is insufficiently small & cannot X Ray Suitcases (dimensions of the baggage scanner is height of 12 inches and width of 20 inches).
X-RAY Machine is not on UPS Backup, therefore, doesn’t provide service in power shut down tenure.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to replace the current Luggage X-Ray machine with a larger model capable of screening suitcases to meet the hotel's security needs. 
Additionally, the X-Ray machine should be connected to a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) backup system to ensure continuous operation during power outages. Regular maintenance and testing of both the X-Ray machine and the UPS system should be conducted to prevent future disruptions and ensure consistent security screening.

observations.title: Discrepancies Observed in Gate Passes Record and Utilization
observations.observation:

Pre-printed, pre-numbered gate passes not used, only computer print of the gate passes is used that is not pre-numbered
Gate passes are only used for the out items, sometimes not in routine, not used for the in items
Complete record of the gate passes not available at the hotel (July-23 to Dec-23 record of the gate passes is not available at hotel)
observations.recommendation: The hotel should implement a proper gate pass system using pre-printed, pre-numbered gate passes for both incoming and outgoing items. Gate passes should be issued consistently, and a complete record must be maintained for verification.

observations.title: Absence of Maintenance Contract for CCTV and Walkthrough Gates
observations.observation: The hotel does not have a maintenance contract for CCTV and walkthrough gates at either the hotel or head office level. Instead of having a fixed contract, maintenance is done on an as-needed basis through local vendors. This approach lacks consistency and may lead to higher costs and delays. A proper maintenance contract should be established, similar to the one made with ESL, to ensure a timely and cost-effective service.
observations.recommendation:
A formal maintenance contract should be established with a reliable vendor for CCTV and walkthrough gates, similar to the contract with ESL. This will ensure timely maintenance, reduce dependency on ad-hoc repairs, and improve equipment reliability.
