observations.title: Employee Attendance not Marked through Biometric Attendance Device
observations.observation:
Employee attendance should be marked through biometric attendance device. On demand of attendance sheet, manual attendance record (Ms. Excel based) was provided by HO HR Department which depicted only present/absent of respective employee in a particular day/date. 
Absence of biometric attendance record of the hotel employees raises several concerns regarding existing payroll management practices/system of the hotel, including the following.
Unavailability of shift wise attendance record (since there are three shifts, moreover night shift allowance detail was also maintained separately as Ms. Excel record).
Unavailability of daily working hours of the employees.
Unauthenticity of employee’s attendance record (as record was manual and editable).
Possibility of errors exists in manual calculation of attendance/night allowance/salaries.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended that the hotel should implement biometric attendance system to accurately track attendance, shifts & shift hours as well as night allowances. This will ensure automated data integrity (calculation of daily working hours, allowances & salaries), minimize errors in payroll processing and calculation, and streamline attendance management, improving overall operational efficiency.
If there are challenges in implementing the biometric attendance system through BEAMS, an efficient solution can be achieved by coordinating with the HR and IT departments.

Store Area

observations.title: No Inspection of Raw Material & Incoming Vehicle/ Missing Certificate of Analysis
observations.observation:
Certificate of Analysis (COA) is a key requirement for compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and other food safety standards. During the audit, it was observed that raw material lots are not consistently inspected in-house upon receipt. There were no records or checklists available to verify that food transportation vehicles comply with hygiene, temperature control, and safety standards before unloading raw materials
Additionally, while suppliers are expected to provide a Certificate of Analysis (COA) for each lot, there is no documented evidence ensuring that COA’s are consistently obtained and verified against internal specification.
observations.recommendation: Ensure that all incoming raw material lots undergo mandatory in-house inspection before use. Develop and implement a standardized checklist for incoming vehicle inspections to ensure compliance with hygiene and safety standards. Additionally, establish a documented procedure requiring suppliers to provide a COA with every lot, and implement a verification process to confirm compliance with internal quality standards

observations.title: No Proper Placement of Storage Racks
observations.observation: Proper Placement of racks is mandatory requirement of standard. These racks must be away from wall and above from floor. During the audit, it was observed that storage racks in the raw material store are placed directly against the wall, contrary to the recommended practice of maintaining a 16-inch gap.
observations.recommendation: Ensure that all storage racks are repositioned to maintain a minimum clearance of 16 inches from the wall. Implement regular monitoring to ensure continued compliance with storage best practices.

observations.title: Food Safety Policy Not Displayed
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the Food Safety Policy was not displayed in the store and raw material receiving area, which is a requirement as per food safety standards. Additionally, there was no evidence of proper communication of the policy to employees
observations.recommendation: Ensure that the food safety policy is clearly displayed in both the store and receiving area. Regularly communicate its importance to staff and conduct periodic checks to ensure visibility and compliance. Conduct regular training sessions to communicate the policy effectively and ensure employees understand their roles in maintaining food safety.

observations.title: No Separate Area for Rejected Items
observations.observation: According to ISO 22000:2018, non-conforming or rejected items must be properly segregated to prevent accidental use and cross-contamination. During the audit, it was observed that the store does not have a designated material rejection area.
observations.recommendation: Establish a dedicated, well-marked material rejection area within the store. Ensure proper signage, clear identification, and staff awareness to facilitate effective handling and segregation of rejected materials. Regular monitoring should be conducted to maintain compliance.

observations.title: Supplier Evaluation not Conducted
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that supplier audits are not being conducted as per the requirements of ISO 22000:2018. During the audit, it was observed that there is no structured supplier approval process in place. Additionally, supplier audits are not conducted on a regular basis to ensure compliance with quality and safety standards.
observations.recommendation: Develop and implement a formal supplier approval process, including predefined criteria for evaluation. Establish a schedule for regular supplier audits to assess compliance, quality standards, and performance. Maintain proper documentation to ensure traceability and accountability.

observations.title: No Defined Raw Material Inspection Criteria
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that there is no defined raw material inspection area in the store, which is a requirement under ISO 22000:2018. The absence of a designated inspection area increases the risk of contaminated, damaged, or non-compliant raw materials being accepted into the production process without proper evaluation.
observations.recommendation: Establish and document clear raw material inspection criteria to ensure consistency in quality checks. Additionally, develop a structured procurement system aligned with standard procurement requirements, including supplier evaluation, material specifications, and approval processes. Regular training and monitoring should be implemented to ensure compliance.

observations.title: Insects Killers & Rodent Traps Seems to be Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that insect and rodent traps were missing at key entry points and storage areas, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 food safety standards.
observations.recommendation: Install rodent traps and insect killers at all entry points to prevent pest intrusion. Implement a comprehensive pest control management system, including regular inspections, proper documentation, and corrective actions. Engage a professional pest control service to ensure compliance with food safety standards.

observations.title: Material Safety Data Sheet Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) were not available for the cleaning chemicals stored in the facility, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and general food safety regulations. MSDS documents are essential for ensuring safe handling, storage, and emergency response procedures for hazardous substances.
observations.recommendation: Ensure that MSDS for all cleaning chemicals are readily available in the store. Train staff on the safe handling and usage of chemicals as per the provided safety guidelines. Conduct regular checks to ensure compliance with chemical safety regulations.

observations.title: No Temperature Guns and Monitoring of Chillers Temperature
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that temperature guns were not available for monitoring food storage and transportation temperatures, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. Proper temperature monitoring is crucial to ensure food safety, prevent spoilage, and maintain the cold chain for perishable items. Moreover, the chiller temperatures are not being consistently monitored and recorded, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Proper temperature control is crucial to prevent food spoilage, bacterial growth, and contamination.
observations.recommendation: Ensure that calibrated temperature guns are available and used for regular temperature monitoring. Implement a routine chiller temperature monitoring system, ensuring that temperatures are checked at regular intervals and recorded systematically Train staff on proper usage and recording of temperature data to maintain compliance with food safety and quality control standards. Conduct periodic checks to verify the functionality.

observations.title: No Proper Documentation Available for Cleaning & Sanitation
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that no proper cleaning and sanitation procedures were in place, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. A structured cleaning and sanitation program are essential to prevent cross-contamination, microbial growth, and food safety hazards.
observations.recommendation: Develop and implement a standardized cleaning and sanitation procedure, including clear guidelines on cleaning frequency, approved chemicals, proper methods, and responsible personnel. Train staff on these procedures and maintain records of cleaning activities to ensure accountability and compliance.

observations.title: No Segregation of Food and Non-Food Material
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that food and non-food items are stored together without proper segregation, and there are no designated racks to separate them, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Proper segregation is essential to prevent cross-contamination and ensure food safety.
observations.recommendation: Designate separate, clearly labelled racks for food and non-food items to prevent cross-contamination. Implement storage guidelines that ensure proper segregation, and train staff on the importance of maintaining food safety standards.

observations.title: Medical Test of Store Staff Found to Be Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that medical tests of store staff are either not conducted or not properly documented, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Ensuring that all food-handling personnel are medically fit is crucial to prevent food contamination and ensure consumer safety.
observations.recommendation: Ensure that all store staff undergo mandatory medical tests at regular intervals as per food safety regulations. Maintain proper records of medical check-ups and fitness certificates.

observations.title: HACCP Documentation Found to Be Missing
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) documents were not available, and there was no evidence of its implementation, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements.
observations.recommendation: Develop and implement a comprehensive HACCP plan, including hazard identification, critical control points (CCPs), monitoring procedures, corrective actions, and record-keeping. Train relevant staff on HACCP principles and ensure ongoing compliance through regular audits and documentation updates.

observations.title: Non-Compliance with Allergen Management Requirements
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that allergens were not properly segregated, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. There were no clear procedures for identifying, handling, or segregating allergenic ingredients.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to develop and implement a structured allergen management system, including proper labeling, storage segregation, and handling procedures for allergenic ingredients. Training should also be provided staff on allergen control measures, and establish clear documentation and monitoring processes to ensure compliance.
Main Kitchen

observations.title: Visitor Entrance Protocols not Found in Kitchen
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that visitor entrance protocols are not properly implemented, which is non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. Visitors are not required to follow specific hygiene and safety measures before accessing food preparation areas.
observations.recommendation: Develop and implement a visitor entrance protocol, including mandatory hygiene practices such as wearing protective gear, handwashing, and signing a visitor log. Clearly display entry requirements at the entrance and train staff on enforcing the protocol. Regular audits should be conducted to ensure compliance.

observations.title: No Allergens Mentioned in Menu
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that allergens are not mentioned in the menu, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. There are no indications or labels identifying potential allergens in food items.
observations.recommendation: Update the menu to clearly indicate allergen information for each dish. Use symbols or labels to highlight common allergens such as nuts, dairy, gluten, and seafood. Train staff on allergen awareness and ensure proper documentation is maintained for compliance with food safety standards.

observations.title: Unavailability No Training Records
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that no training records for employees were found which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. There is no documented evidence of staff training on food safety, hygiene, or operational procedures.
observations.recommendation: Implement a system to record and maintain employee training, ensuring that all staff members receive training in food safety, hygiene, and other necessary areas. Keep up-to-date training logs for all employees and periodically review the training process to ensure compliance with industry standards.

observations.title: Use of Non-Food-Grade Wooden Utensils in Food Handling Areas
observations.observation: It was observed that non-food-grade wooden items are being used in food handling areas, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 & HACCP. Wooden materials are porous and can harbor bacteria, moisture, and contaminants, posing a risk to food safety.
observations.recommendation: Replace all wooden kitchen items with food-grade, non-porous alternatives such as stainless steel or food-safe plastic. Implement a policy prohibiting the use of wooden utensils and surfaces in food preparation areas.

observations.title: Non-Food Graded Sauces Bottles & Packaging Material
observations.observation: It was observed that non-food-grade sauce bottles are being used, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 & HACCP. Ketchup and sauce bottles being used are not food-grade, posing a potential risk of contamination.
observations.recommendation: Ensure that all ketchup and sauce bottles are made of food-grade materials that meet regulatory standards. Replace non-food-grade containers with certified food-safe alternatives.

observations.title: Chillers Temperature not Being Monitored
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that chiller temperatures are not being consistently monitored and recorded, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements. Temperature control is critical for preventing bacterial growth and ensuring food safety.
observations.recommendation: Implement a structured temperature monitoring system for all chillers. Assign staff to regularly check and record chiller temperatures at set intervals. Use calibrated temperature monitoring devices and maintain logs for compliance.

observations.title: Use of Manual Garbage Bins
observations.observation: It was observed that garbage bins are not foot-operated because of these do not meet hygiene standards, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements. In practice they opened the lid of bin with hands. Proper waste disposal practices are essential to prevent cross-contamination, pest infestation, and environmental hazards.
observations.recommendation: Replace existing garbage bins with foot-operated bins to minimize hand contact and reduce the risk of contamination. Ensure that bins are regularly cleaned, covered, and placed in appropriate locations to maintain hygiene.

observations.title: Non-Maintenance of Mandatory Food Safety Records and Logs
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that record-keeping for food safety processes is not maintained, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP requirements. Kitchen staff do not maintain any record forms related to food safety, hygiene, cleaning schedules, temperature logs, or other critical operational procedures.
observations.recommendation: Implement a structured record-keeping system for kitchen staff. Ensure that all critical records, such as temperature logs, cleaning schedules, food preparation checklists, and hygiene audits, are maintained daily. Train staff on the importance of documentation and conduct regular audits to ensure compliance. Digital record-keeping solutions can also be considered for better efficiency and tracking.

observations.title: HACCP Documentation not Maintained
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) documentation is not available, which is a major non-compliance with HACCP principles and ISO 22000:2018 requirements.
observations.recommendation: Develop and implement a HACCP plan, including hazard analysis, critical control points (CCPs), monitoring procedures, corrective actions, verification activities, and record-keeping. Train staff on HACCP principles and ensure proper documentation of all HACCP-related activities. Conduct regular internal audits to assess compliance and maintain food safety standards.

observations.title: Expired Syrup Bottles Found in Kitchen
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that expired syrup bottles were found in the kitchen, which is a serious non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018. This indicates inadequate stock rotation and a lack of monitoring of product shelf life.
observations.recommendation:
Immediately remove and dispose of all expired syrup bottles. Implement a strict First-In, First-Out (FIFO) inventory management system to ensure proper stock rotation. Conduct regular checks on product expiry dates, maintain updated inventory records, and assign staff responsibility for monitoring stock.
Required Documentation

observations.title: Missing Required Documents
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that essential documentation required for ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP compliance was missing. The following critical documents were not found:
Drinking water and process water testing reports from an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved laboratory, covering physiochemical, heavy metals, and microbiological parameters.
Wastewater testing reports for physical and chemical parameters.
Complete documentation of food safety management system, including:
Policies and procedures
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
Monitoring record sheets
observations.recommendation:
Arrange water quality testing from an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved lab and maintain updated reports. 
Conduct wastewater testing and ensure compliance with environmental regulations. 
Develop and implement food safety documentation, including policies, SOPs, and monitoring records. 
Train staff on documentation requirements and ensure proper record-keeping for audits and regulatory compliance. Regularly review and update food safety documents to align with ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP standards.

observations.title: Environmental & Engineering Monitoring Process not in Place
observations.observation:
During the audit, it was observed that environmental and engineering monitoring processes were not in place, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. The following critical parameters were not documented or monitored:
Light Intensity: Section-wise assessment missing.
Noise level: No section-wise monitoring records.
Temperature and Humidity: No documented tracking.
Air Quality Monitoring: Not conducted or recorded.
Generator Stack Emission: No testing or compliance records.
Boiler Stack Emission: Monitoring records not available.
Workers’ Hand Swab Testing: No microbiological testing records.
Processing Equipment Swab Testing: No hygiene validation.
Electrical DBs (Distribution Boards): No inspection or safety records.
Boiler Inspection: No preventive maintenance or safety audit found.
Lift Inspection: No compliance records or maintenance logs.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to:
Implement a structured Environmental & Engineering Monitoring covering all listed parameters. 
Conduct yearly light, noise, temperature, humidity, and air quality assessments and maintain records. 
Perform generator and boiler stack emissions testing to comply with environmental regulations. 
Establish microbiological swab testing protocols for workers' hands and processing equipment. 
Conduct periodic electrical DB, boiler, and lift inspections with proper documentation. 
Train staff on safety and hygiene monitoring and assign responsibilities for maintaining records. 
Ensure all monitoring activities are reviewed periodically for continuous improvement and compliance.

observations.title: Calibration of Measuring and Monitoring Devices not Done
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that the calibration of monitoring and measuring devices and equipment had not been conducted which is non-compliance of ISO 22000:2018. Additionally, there was no evidence of calibration records from an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved laboratory.
observations.recommendation:
It is recommended to:
Schedule calibration for all monitoring and measuring devices (e.g., thermometers, weighing scales, air quality meters, humidity sensors, pH meters) through an ISO 17025 & EPA-approved lab. 
Maintain calibration certificates and records for all critical equipment. 
Implement a calibration schedule to ensure regular monitoring and compliance. 
Train relevant staff on the importance of calibration and ensure proper documentation is maintained for audits and regulatory compliance. 
Conduct periodic internal audits to verify that calibration records are updated and all equipment functions within acceptable limits.

observations.title: Non-Compliance in Laboratory Testing of Raw and Final Products
observations.observation: During the audit, it was observed that final and raw material analysis is not being conducted from an external ISO 17025-accredited laboratory, which is a non-compliance with ISO 22000:2018 requirements. Regular testing of raw materials and final products is essential to ensure food safety, quality, and compliance with regulatory standards.
observations.recommendation:
Conduct regular external laboratory testing from an ISO 17025-accredited lab for the following:
Raw Material Analysis: (Twice a Year)
Fruits & Vegetables: Pesticide residues & heavy metals
Meat Products: Microbiological analysis
Dairy Products: Proximate & microbiological analysis
Dry Food Items (Spices, Pulses, etc.): Aflatoxins, microorganisms, pesticides
Final Product Analysis: (Quarterly)
Cooked & uncooked food testing on a quarterly basis
Comprehensive microbiological analysis
Ensure proper documentation of all test reports for regulatory compliance and traceability.
